item.title: On this day in 1975: David Bowie released <i>Young Americans</i>
item.description: On March 7, 1975, David Bowie released his iconic, Philly soul-inspired seventh album, <i>Young Americans.</i> Highlights of the album include 'Fame', Bowie's first No.1 single – co-written with John Lennon and Carlos Alomar – as well as key contributions from then-little-known singer Luther Vandross. To mark its anniversary, we're revisiting some special reflections on <i>Young Americans,</i> all selected from the <i>Hot Press</i> archives...

item.title: Cabaret Voltaire: "We were never restricted or anchored by the idea of being a pop band – we were more experimental and always tried different things"
item.description: As Sheffield industrial pioneers Cabaret Voltaire mark their 50th anniversary with a farewell tour, Stephen Mallinder discusses their early gigs with Joy Division, influencing Nine Inch Nails, collaborating with rock wild man Al Jourgensen, and the group’s unique association with Ferris Bueller.
